newsitem.title: USA: Builders Square, Hechinger to combine.
newsitem.headline: Builders Square, Hechinger to combine.

text.p: Kmart Corp., Hechinger Co., and Leonard Green & Partners LP said Thursday they had reached a definitive pact to create the nation's third largest home improvement chain by uniting Hechinger with Kmart's Builders Square.

In the deal, valued at about $136.6 million, Leonard Green, a Los Angeles-based investment banking firm, will acquire Hechinger in a cash buyout for $3 a share and will pay Kmart about $10 million for Builders Square.

The combination unites 162 Builders Square stores in the Midwest and Southwest with Hechinger's 117 home improvement stores in the Midwest and on the East Coast, which carry the Hechinger's and Home Quarters names.
The combined entity will have 279 stores in 29 states and the District of Columbia and have combined annual revenues of more than $4.5 billion, the group said.
It will be the third largest U.S. home improvement retailer behind No. 1 Home Depot Inc. and No. 2 Lowe's Cos. Inc..
Leonard Green & Partners will own 100 percent of the new company through an investment partnership. Kmart will receive a warrant to purchase a minority interest at a later date, the group said.
For Troy, Mich.-based Kmart, the deal takes the struggling Builders Square off its hands and completes a more than three-year effort to shed its speciality retail operations.

Kmart investor relations director Robert Burton said the deal will not affect the retailer's bottom line because the discount retailer took a $385 million charge in the fourth quarter of 1996 to write off its investment in the San Antonio-based unit.
"The benefit to Kmart shareholders is that this agreement creates an operating business that can successfully assume the obligations for the store leases," he said.
Hechinger Chief Financial Officer W. Clark McClelland told Reuters in an interview that the company will maintain Hechinger's Largo, Md., headquarters and may close some redundant stores.
"It gives the company substantial purchasing power and the opportunity to reduce expenses, particularly in the general administrative area," he said. "There's a fair amount of synergies."

Holders of the 42.2 million Hechinger Class A and Class B shares will receive $3 cash per share under the deal, which Hechinger said represents a 100 percent premium over the Class A price the week before the announcement of a possible transaction.

The group said Anthony Petrillo will serve as acting chief executive of the new company. Petrillo has more than 35 years of experience in retail and has worked with Leonard Green & Partners in its retailing portfolio companies since 1994.

Leonard Green said it has provided the new company with financial flexibility to commit significant capital to refurbish, remodel and remerchandise its stores to improve customer service and revitalise its business.
Financing is being arranged by Chase Manhattan Corp. in conjunction with BankAmerica Business Credit Inc. and Citicorp USA Inc., a subsidiary of Citibank.
The deal is subject to customary regulatory approvals, bank financing and approval by Hechinger shareholders.
Hechinger Class A shares closed Thursday down 12.5 cents at $2 on Nasdaq. Its Class B shares closed unchanged at $3. Kmart closed unchanged at $10.69 on the New York Stock Exchange.
